show_title: Architects & Builders: The Business History of the Global African Diaspora
title: Frank McWorter: He Bought His Wife First, Then Platted a Town
summary: Frank McWorter turned Kentucky saltpeter into family freedom, then platted New Philadelphia, Illinois, the first U.S. town registered by an African American.
description:
Frank “Free Frank” McWorter mined saltpeter in Kentucky while enslaved, paid for his pregnant wife’s freedom before his own, and in 1836 platted New Philadelphia, Illinois, the first U.S. town platted and registered by an African American. Lessons for operators on sequencing liabilities, buying into legal exemptions early, subdivision, and the routing risk that bypassed his town.

Read the full analysis on The Black Executive Journal: https://www.blackexecutivebrief.com/frank-mcworter-the-developer-who-bought-his-wife-first-and-platted-a-town-to-pay-for-the-rest/

A Yesterday's Architects episode.
